successCriteria.description: `LeaveRequestView` in web/src/shared/types/index.ts declares `reversesRequestId: string | null` as its LAST field, positioned after `cancelledAt`; no other field of that interface is added, renamed, split, reordered, or retyped.
`npm run build` (tsc) completes clean for BOTH application roots (the Fastify service under src/ and the React app under web/src/), with no new type errors introduced.
The existing Jest suite still passes unchanged (no test file added, modified, or deleted this phase).

The leave list read path returns BOTH the original APPROVED row and its CANCELLED reversal row as two independent entries, each carrying `reversesRequestId` (the original row's value is null; the reversal row's value is the original row's id) — neither row is suppressed, collapsed, or filtered out.

The single-request read path returns the same `reversesRequestId` value for a given row that the list path returns for that row (no route-level remapping or divergence between the two read endpoints).

constraints: The new field MUST be named exactly `reversesRequestId` and typed `string | null` on the web read model, matching the backend `LeaveRequest` field name and nullability — do not invent a different name or a non-nullable type.

`reversesRequestId` MUST be the LAST field of `LeaveRequestView`; no other field of `LeaveRequestView` may be added, renamed, split, reordered, or retyped, and `EmployeeProfile`, `LeaveBalanceView`, `LoginResponse`, `CreateLeaveRequestInput`, and all enums must be left untouched.

No client-side reversal logic may be introduced: `web/src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts` (`ILeaveService`/`LeaveService`), `leave.actions.ts`, and `leave.validation.ts` keep their existing method set and behaviour; the new field only flows through `LeaveRequestView`.

The read path's role scoping MUST NOT change: `GET /leaves` continues to return both the original APPROVED row and its CANCELLED reversal row as two independent entries, and the client pairs them via `reversesRequestId`. Suppressing the original would break the immutable-row-is-still-readable contract GP-008 protects.

No query parameter may be added to the read endpoints, and no route-level mapping may be added: the repository's `mapRow` already supplies the field, so the route must pass the service's `LeaveRequest` objects through unchanged. If no route change is required, leave `src/modules/leave/leave.routes.ts` untouched rather than inventing one.
The phase edits at most the two named files (`web/src/shared/types/index.ts` and, only if required, `src/modules/leave/leave.routes.ts`); no test files change this phase.
outOfScope: The reversal unit test and smoke assertion (Phase 4) — no test file changes this phase.
Any client-side reversal logic or pairing/grouping behaviour in `leave.service.ts`, `leave.actions.ts`, or `leave.validation.ts` — the field only flows through `LeaveRequestView`.
Any change to the read path's role scoping, query parameters, or suppression/collapsing of either the original APPROVED row or its CANCELLED reversal row.
Any change to `EmployeeProfile`, `LeaveBalanceView`, `LoginResponse`, `CreateLeaveRequestInput`, or any enum in the web shared types.
Backend model/repository/schema changes for `reversesRequestId` — delivered in Phase 1 and assumed present.

ambiguities.description: Whether `src/modules/leave/leave.routes.ts` requires any edit at all, or should be left untouched.
options: Leave the file untouched — the repository's mapRow already supplies the field and the route passes service objects through unchanged
Add a route-level mapping to explicitly surface the field

ambiguities.description: Whether the web read model should expose the reversal linkage as a nullable self-reference only, or also carry any derived pairing/grouping helper.
options: Expose only the nullable `reversesRequestId` field; no derived helpers (per phase scope)
Add a derived pairing helper on the read model

entityInvariants.invariant: Mirrors the backend `LeaveRequest` read shape field-for-field; the reversal linkage is exposed as a nullable self-reference so a client can distinguish the original APPROVED row (null) from its CANCELLED reversal row (the original's id). It is a read-only projection — it carries no lifecycle transitions and no client-side reversal behaviour.

A CANCELLED reversal row is terminal and immutable, carries the original's request shape verbatim, and is linked back to the original APPROVED row via `reversesRequestId`. The original APPROVED row remains readable and unmodified (GP-008); both rows are independently returned by the read path.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Existing role scoping unchanged: EMPLOYEE sees own requests, MANAGER sees own + direct reports, ADMIN sees all. No new query parameter and no change to the scoping filter.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Unchanged — existing typed errors (Unauthorized/Forbidden/Validation) propagate as before; the new field introduces no new error path.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Existing visibility rule unchanged (owner, direct manager, or ADMIN); no change to the scoping logic.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Unchanged — NotFound for invisible/absent rows as before; the new field introduces no new error path.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The web `LeaveRequestView.reversesRequestId` field name, type (`string | null`), and nullability MUST match the backend `LeaveRequest.reversesRequestId` field exactly, so the read model is a faithful projection of the service's returned object.
The value surfaced on the read model MUST originate from the repository's row mapping (`reverses_request_id` -> `reversesRequestId`); the route must not re-derive, rename, or remap it.

The read endpoints MUST continue to return the service's `LeaveRequest` objects unchanged (both the original APPROVED row and its CANCELLED reversal row), preserving the existing role scoping and the immutable-row-is-still-readable contract.
The web leave service/actions/validation MUST keep their existing method set and behaviour; the new field flows through `LeaveRequestView` without any client-side reversal logic being added.

integrationPoints.why: The API client returns `LeaveRequestView` from every leave read/write call; adding the field to the shared type makes it available to all consumers without changing the client.
Delegates verbatim to the API client and returns `LeaveRequestView`; the new field flows through unchanged with no method-set change.
`mapRow` supplies `reversesRequestId` from `reverses_request_id`; this is the single source of the value the read path exposes.
The read endpoints pass the service's `LeaveRequest` objects through; the field must reach the wire unchanged, with no route-level mapping or query param added.
